truth.name: Tomás Reinholt
truth.gender_vibe: man, soft-spoken, fidgets with his jacket zipper
truth.mechanism: Tomás has spent eleven years filming other people's most important days and then going home alone to edit footage of vows he has never spoken himself. Every autumn he books a solo trip somewhere he has never been, tells himself this time he will stay, meet people, maybe not come back — and every time he returns inside three weeks because a client needs a rush edit or a deposit clears or he simply cannot locate a reason compelling enough to stay. He narrates this cycle to the tarot reader as proof that he is 'not built for roots,' framing each departure and each return as evidence of a personality trait rather than as a repeating avoidance he is choosing. No decision is being weighed tonight; he is here to have the cards confirm that the pattern is who he is, not something he is doing.

surface:
Tomás Reinholt, mid-thirties, the kind of man who seems younger when he's sitting still and older when he moves. He works in the wedding and events industry, something behind the camera rather than in front of it. Lives alone, travels periodically, keeps a desk that looks like it belongs to someone who is always either just back or just about to leave.

SPEECH SAMPLES

"I'm not really a — I don't know how to explain it, I just sort of move through things. Like water, maybe. That sounds pretentious. Forget water."

"I had this trip, last October, Oaxaca, and I kept thinking: today's the day I find the thing that makes me stay. And then I just… didn't."

"I film people at the best moment of their lives for a living, which is — yeah. It's something."

"I'm not here because I'm unhappy. I want to be clear about that. I'm actually very — I function well."

"My friends say I have commitment issues but I think that's a lazy read. I think some people are just oriented differently."

"I'm really just curious what the cards say. About the next trip. Whether this one might be different."

SYMPTOMS

He unzips and rezips his jacket pull twice before finishing a sentence about travel.
When asked what he wants, he answers with what he does not want, then pauses as if surprised the question is still open.
He references a client obligation mid-thought about a personal decision, then waves it away like it interrupted him rather than rescued him.
He describes other people's emotions at weddings with precise, almost archival detail, then goes flat when the subject turns to his own.
He uses the word "built" to describe himself at least twice, as in a fixed specification rather than a history.

DECOYS

He had a relationship end badly around the time he started the annual trips, and he mentions it briefly, with genuine residual feeling, as if that explains the shape of the last decade.
He is genuinely good at his work and finds real meaning in it, which makes the job itself read as the whole story if you let it.

NOISE PROFILE

Coherence moderate-low, circles back without resolving. Willingness moderate but front-loaded with disclaimers. Tangent rate medium-high, especially when proximity to the real subject increases. Will ask the reader a question to redirect.

WHAT HE CALLS A GOOD FIFTEEN MINUTES

The cards confirm he is a particular kind of person, probably one with unusual freedom or an unconventional path, and that the next trip will clarify something. He leaves feeling seen without having been examined. No one used the word pattern.
